questions.question_english: Under the standard financial procedures and Treasury Rules governing the preparation of monthly salary bills, which of the following is NOT an authorized deduction from the monthly salary of a Government servant?
options_english: Direct recovery of commercial bank personal loan EMI without a court attachment order or employee consent
Mandatory deduction of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) under statutory Income Tax provisions
Compulsory monthly subscription/contribution towards General Provident Fund (GPF) or National Pension System (NPS)
Recovery of standard monthly licence fee for allotment of official government residential accommodation
questions.explanation_english: Authorized deductions from the salary bill of a government employee are strictly governed by Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, Treasury Rules, and Civil Services Regulations. Permissible statutory and authorized deductions include: (1) Statutory deductions like Income Tax (TDS), (2) Subscriptions to GPF, CPF, or NPS, (3) Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme (CGEGIS / DGEHS), (4) Licence fee for government accommodation, (5) Recoveries of advances/loans sanctioned by the Government (computer advance, festival advance, etc.), and (6) Court attachment orders issued under Section 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). A Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) or Head of School has no statutory legal authority to recover personal loan installments of private/commercial banks or third parties from an employee's salary bill unless backed by a formal decree/attachment order of a competent court or explicit statutory authorization.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सरकार लेखा (प्राप्ति एवं भुगतान) नियमावली तथा ट्रेजरी नियमों के अनुसार, सरकारी कर्मचारी के वेतन बिल से केवल वही कटौतियां की जा सकती हैं जो विधिवत अधिकृत या सांविधिक हों। इनमें शामिल हैं: (1) सांविधिक कटौतियां जैसे आयकर (TDS), (2) GPF या NPS में अनिवार्य अंशदान, (3) समूह बीमा योजना (CGEGIS/DGEHS), (4) सरकारी आवास का लाइसेंस शुल्क (लाइसेंस फीस), (5) सरकार द्वारा स्वीकृत अग्रिमों/ऋणों की वसूली, तथा (6) सिविल प्रक्रिया संहिता (CPC) की धारा 60 के तहत सक्षम न्यायालय द्वारा जारी कुर्की आदेश (Court Attachment Order)। बिना न्यायालय के आदेश या वैध सहमति के किसी वाणिज्यिक/निजी बैंक के व्यक्तिगत ऋण की किस्त वेतन से काटना पूरी तरह अनाधिकृत और वित्तीय नियमों का गंभीर उल्लंघन है।

questions.question_english: Under the statutory provisions of Fundamental Rule 9(21)(a) [FR 9(21)], the technical definition of 'Pay' includes:
options_english: Basic Pay together with Dearness Allowance and full House Rent Allowance entitlements
Basic Pay, Transport Allowance, and Children Education Allowance components
Gross monthly salary inclusive of all sanctioned regular and compensatory allowances
Basic Pay in the sanctioned scale, Special Pay, and Personal Pay
questions.explanation_english: According to Fundamental Rule 9(21)(a)(i), 'Pay' means the amount drawn monthly by a Government servant as: (i) The pay, other than special pay or pay granted in view of personal qualifications, which has been sanctioned for a post held by him substantively or in an officiating capacity, or to which he is entitled by reason of his position in a cadre; (ii) Overseas pay, special pay and personal pay; and (iii) Any other emoluments which may be specially classed as pay by the President. Under the rules, compensatory allowances (such as Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, Transport Allowance, Non-Practicing Allowance unless specified, or City Compensatory Allowance) are categorized as 'Compensatory Allowances' under FR 9(5) and are expressly excluded from the core definition of 'Pay'. Hence, 'Pay' strictly comprises Basic Pay, Special Pay, and Personal Pay.
questions.explanation_hindi: मूल नियमावली [Fundamental Rule 9(21)(a)] के अंतर्गत 'वेतन' (Pay) की सांविधिक परिभाषा में शामिल है: (1) किसी पद पर मौलिक अथवा स्थानापन्न (Officiating) रूप से कार्य करते हुए आहरित मूल वेतन (Basic Pay), (2) विशिष्ट अथवा अत्यधिक कठिन दायित्वों के निर्वहन हेतु स्वीकृत विशेष वेतन (Special Pay), (3) किसी कर्मचारी को वेतन में हानि से बचाने के लिए दिया गया व्यक्तिगत वेतन (Personal Pay), तथा (4) कोई अन्य परिलब्धियां जिन्हें राष्ट्रपति द्वारा 'वेतन' के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया हो। महंगाई भत्ता (DA), मकान किराया भत्ता (HRA) तथा परिवहन भत्ता (TA) जैसी मदें FR 9(5) के तहत 'प्रतिपूरक भत्तों' (Compensatory Allowances) की श्रेणी में आती हैं और वे 'वेतन' की मूल परिभाषा में शामिल नहीं होती हैं। अतः सही विकल्प Basic Pay, Special Pay और Personal Pay है।
questions.topic: DoE Directorate of Education, Delhi: Circulars and Guidelines
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Basic Pay, Special Pay, and Personal Pay

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Fundamental Rule 9(21)(a), the statutory definition of pay includes the basic pay drawn in the prescribed scale, special pay granted for specific arduous duties, and personal pay granted to save an employee from salary loss. Compensatory allowances such as Dearness Allowance or House Rent Allowance are excluded.

questions.question_english: According to the regulatory guidelines issued by the Directorate of Education (DoE) for admission to entry-level classes in private unaided recognized schools of Delhi, which of the following admission criteria is strictly prohibited?
options_english: Education qualification of the parents
Distance of the student’s residence from the school
Sibling currently studying in the same school
Alumni status of the parents
questions.explanation_english: Admission guidelines issued annually by the Directorate of Education (DoE), GNCTD, under the Delhi School Education Act & Rules, 1973, and Section 13(1) of the RTE Act, 2009, strictly prohibit discriminatory and arbitrary admission criteria for entry-level classes (Pre-school/Nursery, Pre-primary/KG, and Class I). Specifically, criteria evaluating the educational qualifications, profession, income, oral test/interview, or background profiling of parents are categorically barred. The guidelines permit only rational, objective, and non-discriminatory criteria such as neighbourhood proximity (distance points), siblings currently enrolled in the school, and alumni status. Screening procedures or interviews for children or parents attract statutory penalties under Section 13(2) of the RTE Act, 2009.
questions.explanation_hindi: शिक्षा निदेशालय (DoE), दिल्ली सरकार द्वारा दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम और नियम (DSEAR), 1973 तथा निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 13(1) के तहत निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त मान्यता प्राप्त विद्यालयों में प्रवेश-स्तरीय कक्षाओं (नर्सरी/केजी/कक्षा 1) में प्रवेश हेतु सख्त दिशा-निर्देश जारी किए जाते हैं। इन दिशा-निर्देशों के तहत अभिभावकों की शैक्षणिक योग्यता, साक्षात्कार, मौखिक परीक्षा, वित्तीय स्थिति अथवा व्यवसाय के आधार पर प्रोफाइलिंग करने पर पूर्णतः प्रतिबंध है। विद्यालयों को केवल वस्तुनिष्ठ और गैर-भेदभावपूर्ण मानदंड अपनाने की अनुमति है, जैसे निकटता/पड़ोस (दूरी के अंक), सगा सहोदर (सगा भाई/बहन विद्यालय में अध्ययनरत होना), और पूर्व छात्र (Alumni) कोटा। RTE अधिनियम की धारा 13(2) के तहत स्क्रीनिंग प्रक्रिया अपनाने पर भारी आर्थिक जुर्माने का वैधानिक प्रावधान है।

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The Principal / Vice Principal of a Delhi government school can be formally declared and serve as the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) for that school.
Reason (R): Under the Receipts and Payments Rules and Treasury Rules, the Drawing and Disbursing Officer is responsible for preparing, signing, and presenting financial bills to the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO) and maintaining proper custody and accounts of cash drawn.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: Under Rule 3 of the Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, 1983 and Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR), a Head of Department / Competent Authority in the Directorate of Education may designate a Gazetted Officer (such as the Principal or Vice-Principal / Head of School) to function as the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) for an institution.
Reason (R) is also true: By statutory definition under financial rules, a DDO is a designated officer entrusted with drawing money, presenting bills to the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO), and maintaining primary financial registers such as the Cash Book.
However, Reason (R) merely defines the administrative duties and functional role of a DDO; it does NOT explain the administrative rationale for *why* a Principal is appointed as a DDO (which is rooted in administrative decentralization and delegation of financial powers to the Head of Office to facilitate local institutional governance). Therefore, both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) सत्य है: केंद्रीय सरकारी लेखा (प्राप्ति एवं संदाय) नियमावली, 1983 के नियम 3 तथा वित्तीय शक्तियों के प्रत्यायोजन नियम (DFPR) के अंतर्गत, शिक्षा निदेशालय का सक्षम प्राधिकारी किसी विद्यालय के राजपत्रित अधिकारी (प्रधानाचार्य या उप-प्रधानाचार्य) को उस संस्था का आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) घोषित कर सकता है।
कारण (R) भी सत्य है: वित्तीय नियमों के तहत DDO का विधिक उत्तरदायित्व वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) में बिल प्रस्तुत करना, सरकारी धन का आहरण करना तथा रोकड़ बही (Cash Book) का समुचित संधारण करना होता है।
तथापि, कारण (R) DDO के कर्तव्यों और परिभाषा का वर्णन करता है, किंतु यह इस बात का तार्किक या प्रशासनिक कारण स्पष्ट नहीं करता कि प्रधानाचार्य को ही DDO क्यों बनाया जाता है (जिसका वास्तविक कारण स्थानीय संस्थागत वित्तीय स्वायत्तता और प्रशासनिक विकेंद्रीकरण है)। अतः A और R दोनों सत्य हैं, लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

questions.question_english: In the context of government financial administration and the preparation of budget estimates, the term 'Revised Estimates' (RE) specifically denotes:
options_english: The initial annual budgetary funds demanded by the school administration at the beginning of the financial year
The projected expected receipts and operational expenditure formulated for the ensuing financial year
The special supplementary grant sanctioned directly by the Central Government to meet unforeseen deficits
An estimate of probable receipts and expenditure for the current financial year based on actuals of the initial months
questions.explanation_english: In government accounting and public budgeting (governed by General Financial Rules 2017 and the Budget Manual), 'Revised Estimates' (RE) are estimates of probable receipts and expenditure for the current financial year. They are framed midway through the financial year by taking into account the actual expenditure and receipts of the initial months (usually April to September/October) and the anticipated requirements for the remaining part of the year. While Revised Estimates do not authorize expenditure by themselves (which requires formal supplementary grants or appropriation if exceeding original Budget Estimates), they serve as a critical re-assessment tool for the Finance Department and the Directorate of Education to redistribute funds and adjust allocations.

questions.explanation_english: Under the operational guidelines of the PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) Scheme issued by the Ministry of Education and enforced by circulars of the Directorate of Education, Delhi, food safety and quality assurance protocols are non-negotiable. The tasting observations regarding temperature, taste, smell, and cleanliness are recorded and signed daily in the statutory 'PM POSHAN Tasting Register'. Hence, Assertion (A) is true, and Reason (R) correctly explains the safety rationale behind mandatory testing.

questions.question_english: According to the Delhi School Education Act (DSEA), 1973, what is the statutory provision regarding 'Capitation Fee'?
options_english: It is completely prohibited.
It can be charged only for admissions in Class I.
It can be charged with the prior approval of the SMC.

questions.explanation_english:
1. **Prohibition under DSEA, 1973**: Under **Section 13 of the Delhi School Education Act (DSEA), 1973**, no recognized school—whether government, aided, or unaided private—shall charge any capitation fee or accept any donation or contribution from any parent or student as a condition of admission.
2. **Prohibition under RTE Act, 2009**: This absolute prohibition is further reinforced by **Section 13(1) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009**, which states: *"No school or person shall, while admitting a child, collect any capitation fee and subject the child or his or her parents or guardian to any screening procedure."*
3. **Penal Consequences**: Under Section 13(2)(a) of the RTE Act, charging capitation fees is punishable with a fine which may extend to *ten times* the capitation fee charged. Under DSEA 1973, collecting unauthorized donations or capitation fees invites suspension of school recognition and derecognition proceedings by the Directorate of Education.
questions.explanation_hindi:
1. **DSEA 1973 के तहत वैधानिक प्रतिबंध:** **दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम, 1973 की धारा 13** के अनुसार, किसी भी मान्यता प्राप्त स्कूल (सरकारी, सहायता प्राप्त या गैर-सहायता प्राप्त निजी स्कूल) द्वारा प्रवेश के समय किसी भी प्रकार की कैपिटेशन फीस, दान या चंदा लेना **पूर्णतः प्रतिबंधित** है।
2. **RTE अधिनियम, 2009 का सुदृढ़ीकरण:** RTE अधिनियम की **धारा 13(1)** भी आदेश देती है कि कोई भी स्कूल या व्यक्ति किसी बच्चे को प्रवेश देते समय कोई कैपिटेशन फीस नहीं लेगा और न ही बच्चे या अभिभावक की कोई स्क्रीनिंग परीक्षा लेगा।
3. **दंडात्मक परिणाम:** RTE अधिनियम की धारा 13(2)(a) के तहत कैपिटेशन फीस वसूलने पर ली गई राशि के दस गुना तक का जुर्माना लगाया जा सकता है। इसके अलावा DSEA 1973 के तहत स्कूल की मान्यता रद्द (Derecognition) की जा सकती है।

questions.question_english: Which rule of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 outlines the fundamental principles of public buying, ensuring efficiency, economy, and transparency?

Rule 149
Rule 154
Rule 155
questions.explanation_english: Rule 144 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, codifies the 'Fundamental principles of public buying'. It mandates that every authority delegated financial powers to procure goods in public interest must ensure: (a) description of goods does not favor any particular supplier; (b) procurement specifications meet the technical requirements without superfluous features; (c) criteria for evaluation are clearly specified in advance; and (d) fair, transparent, and equitable treatment is accorded to all bidders to ensure economy and efficiency. By contrast, Rule 149 governs procurement through the GeM portal, Rule 154 governs direct purchase without quotations up to Rs. 25,000, and Rule 155 governs purchases by a Local Purchase Committee up to Rs. 2,50,000.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 का नियम 144 सार्वजनिक खरीद के 'मूलभूत सिद्धांतों' (Fundamental principles of public buying) को प्रतिपादित करता है। यह नियम स्पष्ट करता है कि सार्वजनिक धन से खरीद करने वाले किसी भी अधिकारी को दक्षता (Efficiency), मितव्ययिता (Economy), निष्पक्ष प्रतिस्पर्धा और पारदर्शिता के उच्चतम मानकों का पालन करना होगा। खरीद के विनिर्देश वस्तुपरक होने चाहिए ताकि किसी विशिष्ट विक्रेता को अनुचित लाभ न मिले। इसके विपरीत, नियम 149 गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस (GeM) के माध्यम से खरीद से संबंधित है, नियम 154 बिना कोटेशन के ₹25,000 तक की सीधी खरीद से संबंधित है, तथा नियम 155 स्थानीय खरीद समिति (LPC) द्वारा खरीद का नियमन करता है। अतः सही उत्तर नियम 144 है।

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 66 of the Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, 1983 (Form GAR 17 / TR 22), the Pay Bill Register (PBR) is the core statutory ledger maintained by the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) in every school and government establishment. The PBR contains designated ledger pages for every employee covering the entire financial year. It meticulously records the monthly basic pay, Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA), and all statutory deductions and recoveries including General Provident Fund (GPF) / National Pension System (NPS), Income Tax (TDS), Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme (CGEGIS), Delhi Government Employees Health Scheme (DGEHS), license fees for government accommodation, and recoveries of personal loans/advances. The PBR is the primary accounting document used for reconciliation with the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO), issuance of Form 16, and post-audit verification. The Service Book records biographical and service history, while Stock Registers track inventory.

questions.question_english: Under Section 23 of which specific enactment is a Head of School / Principal legally obligated to ensure that the identity (including name, address, photograph, or school details) of a child who is a victim of a sexual offence is strictly protected from disclosure in any media or public forum?
options_english: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012
Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009
Delhi School Education Act and Rules (DSEAR), 1973
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012:
1. Section 23 strictly prohibits the disclosure of identity of a child victim. It mandates that no report in any newspaper, magazine, television broadcast, internet, or other media format shall disclose the identity of a child, including the child's name, address, photograph, family details, school, neighbourhood, or any other particulars which may lead to the identification of the child.
2. Any person (including school authorities or media) who violates Section 23 is liable for punishment with imprisonment of not less than six months which may extend to one year, or with fine, or both.
3. Furthermore, under Section 19 of the POCSO Act, any school staff member or Head of School who has knowledge of any sexual assault or abuse involving a minor has a mandatory statutory duty to report the incident immediately to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or the local police station. Failure to report under Section 21 attracts imprisonment up to 6 months or fine.
Therefore, the POCSO Act, 2012 governs this mandatory confidentiality, making option (b) correct.

questions.question_english: Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, what specific class of pension is sanctioned to a permanent Government servant who seeks and is permitted voluntary retirement after completing twenty (20) years of qualifying service?
options_english: Invalid Pension
Retiring Pension
Superannuation Pension
Compassionate Allowance
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 36 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972 (and corresponding provisions of CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021), a 'Retiring Pension' is granted to a government servant who retires or is retired in advance of the age of superannuation in accordance with the provisions of Rule 48 or 48-A of these rules or Rule 56 of Fundamental Rules. Under Rule 48-A, a government servant who has completed 20 years of qualifying service may seek voluntary retirement by giving three months' notice in writing to the appointing authority and is eligible for a Retiring Pension based on qualifying service. In contrast, 'Superannuation Pension' (Rule 35) is granted only upon attaining the statutory age of superannuation (60 years); 'Invalid Pension' (Rule 38) is granted when an employee is medically incapacitated from further service; and 'Compassionate Allowance' (Rule 41) is a discretionary grant given to dismissed or removed employees.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियमावली के नियम 36 (तथा सीसीएस पेंशन नियम 2021 के प्रासंगिक नियम) के तहत 'सेवानिवृत्ति पेंशन' (Retiring Pension) उस सरकारी कर्मचारी को दी जाती है जो अधिवर्षिता (सुपरएंनुएशन - 60 वर्ष) की आयु प्राप्त करने से पूर्व नियम 48 या नियम 48-A अथवा FR 56 के अंतर्गत स्वैच्छिक सेवानिवृत्ति लेता है। नियम 48-A के अनुसार 20 वर्ष की अर्हक सेवा पूर्ण कर चुका सरकारी सेवक तीन माह का लिखित नोटिस देकर स्वैच्छिक सेवानिवृत्ति प्राप्त कर सकता है और वह 'रिटायरिंग पेंशन' का हकदार होता है। वहीं, 'अधिवर्षिता पेंशन' 60 वर्ष की पूर्ण आयु पर मिलती है; 'अशक्तता पेंशन' (Invalid Pension) चिकित्सकीय रूप से स्थायी असमर्थ होने पर दी जाती है; तथा सेवा से बर्खास्त या निष्कासित कर्मचारी को पेंशन जब्त होने पर 'अनुकंपा भत्ता' (Compassionate Allowance) दिया जाता है।

questions.question_english: Under Rule 172 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, an 'Advance payment' made to a private firm for the procurement of goods or execution of services should not normally exceed:
questions.question_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 172 के तहत, वस्तुओं की खरीद या सेवाओं के निष्पादन हेतु किसी निजी फर्म को किया जाने वाला 'अग्रिम भुगतान' (Advance payment) सामान्यतः किससे अधिक नहीं होना चाहिए?
options_english: 10% of the contract value
30% of the contract value
50% of the contract value
100% of the contract value
options_hindi: अनुबंध मूल्य का 10%
अनुबंध मूल्य का 30%
अनुबंध मूल्य का 50%
अनुबंध मूल्य का 100%
questions.explanation_english:
Rule 172 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 governs 'Advance payment to supplier' in government departments and educational institutions:

1. Statutory Ceiling for Private Suppliers: Ordinarily, payment for services rendered or supplies made should be released only after the services have been rendered or supplies have been received. However, in unavoidable situations, advance payments to private suppliers can be sanctioned, which should not normally exceed thirty percent (30%) of the total contract value.
2. Specialized Ceilings: For fabrication contracts or turnkey execution projects, advance payment may extend up to 40% of the contract value. For government agencies, Central/State PSUs, or against dispatch documents through bank, advance up to 100% may be permitted.
3. Mandatory Bank Guarantee: Whenever any advance payment is made to a private firm, the procuring authority/DDO must obtain an unconditional and irrevocable Bank Guarantee or equivalent security covering the entire advance amount plus interest to safeguard public exchequer funds against supplier default.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 का नियम 172 सरकारी विभागों और शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में आपूर्तिकर्ताओं को अग्रिम भुगतान को विनियमित करता है:

1. निजी फर्मों हेतु वैधानिक सीमा: सरकारी वित्तीय नियमों का सामान्य सिद्धांत यह है कि वस्तुओं/सेवाओं की प्राप्ति के उपरांत ही भुगतान किया जाए। लेकिन अपरिहार्य परिस्थितियों में, किसी निजी आपूर्तिकर्ता फर्म को दिया जाने वाला अग्रिम भुगतान सामान्यतः कुल अनुबंध मूल्य के तीस प्रतिशत (30%) से अधिक नहीं होना चाहिए।
2. विशेष अनुबंधों में सीमा: निर्माण/फैब्रिकेशन या टर्न-की परियोजनाओं के लिए अग्रिम सीमा 40% तक हो सकती है। सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उपक्रमों (PSUs) अथवा सरकारी एजेंसियों को 100% तक अग्रिम दिया जा सकता है।
3. बैंक गारंटी की अनिवार्यता: निजी फर्म को अग्रिम राशि का भुगतान करते समय आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) द्वारा सार्वजनिक धन की सुरक्षा हेतु अग्रिम राशि के समतुल्य बैंक गारंटी (Bank Guarantee) प्राप्त करना अनिवार्य होता है।

questions.question_english: Under the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules], which authority is competent to impose a major penalty on a Government servant?
options_english: The Inquiry Officer appointed to conduct disciplinary proceedings
The Presenting Officer nominated to represent the department
The Chief Vigilance Officer of the organization
The designated Disciplinary Authority or Appointing Authority
questions.explanation_english:
Under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, and Article 311 of the Constitution of India:

1. Nature of Major Penalties: Major penalties (Rule 11) include reduction to a lower stage/time-scale/grade/post, compulsory retirement, removal from service, and dismissal from service.
2. Constitutional Safeguard: Article 311(1) of the Constitution mandates that no person holding a civil post shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which they were appointed.
3. Competent Authority: Under Rule 12 and Rule 14, major penalties can only be imposed by the Appointing Authority or a designated Disciplinary Authority competent to impose major penalties.
4. Role of Others:
   - The Inquiry Officer (IO) is merely a fact-finding quasi-judicial officer tasked with inquiring into the charges and submitting an inquiry report.
   - The Presenting Officer (PO) acts as a prosecutor on behalf of the department.
   - The Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) provides vigilance advisory opinions.
Neither the IO, PO, nor CVO holds statutory quasi-judicial power to award penalties.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण एवं अपील) नियम, 1965 और भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 311 के तहत:

1. बड़ी शास्तियों का स्वरूप: नियम 11 के तहत बड़ी शास्तियों (Major Penalties) में निचले वेतनमान/पद पर अवनति, अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति, सेवा से हटाया जाना (Removal) और सेवा से बर्खास्तगी (Dismissal) शामिल हैं।
2. संवैधानिक संरक्षण: अनुच्छेद 311(1) के अनुसार, किसी भी सिविल सेवक को उसके नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी (Appointing Authority) से अधीनस्थ किसी प्राधिकारी द्वारा हटाया या बर्खास्त नहीं किया जा सकता।
3. सक्षम प्राधिकारी: केवल अधिकृत अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी (Disciplinary Authority) या नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी ही बड़ी शास्ति लगाने का आदेश पारित कर सकते हैं।
4. अन्य अधिकारियों की भूमिका:
   - जांच अधिकारी (IO) केवल आरोपों की निष्पक्ष जांच कर निष्कर्ष रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करता है।
   - प्रस्तुतकर्ता अधिकारी (PO) विभाग की ओर से साक्ष्य व गवाह प्रस्तुत करता है।
   - मुख्य सतर्कता अधिकारी (CVO) सतर्कता संबंधी सलाह प्रदान करता है।
इनमें से किसी के पास भी दंडादेश पारित करने का विधिक अधिकार नहीं होता।

questions.question_english: Under the Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, 1983 and General Financial Rules (GFR), when a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) or Cashier detects a clerical or computational error in the school Cash Book, what is the mandatory prescribed procedure for rectifying it?
options_english: Applying white correction fluid over the incorrect entry and writing the revised figure neatly over the dried layer
Drawing a single neat line across the incorrect entry in red ink, writing the correct figure above it, and attesting it with dated initials
Completely erasing or scraping out the incorrect figure using an ink eraser or razor blade and writing the fresh entry
Neatly cutting out or tearing off the affected ledger folio page from the bound register and replacing it with a fresh handwritten folio
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 13 of the Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, 1983, erasures, overwriting, and the use of correction fluid in any official account book, particularly the Cash Book (Form GAR 3), are strictly prohibited as they constitute serious financial irregularities. If an error is detected, the prescribed accounting method is to strike through the incorrect entry with a single neat line (traditionally in red ink) in such a manner that the original figure remains legible, write the correct entry above it, and have the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) attest the correction by putting their dated initials. Tearing or removing pages from a bound, page-numbered Cash Book is a punishable offense under government accounting rules.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सरकारी लेखा (प्राप्ति एवं संदाय) नियमावली, 1983 के नियम 13 के अनुसार, रोकड़ बही (Cash Book - Form GAR 3) या किसी भी वित्तीय अभिलेख में प्रविष्टियों को खुरचना, मिटाना, ओवरराइटिंग करना या व्हाइटनर/सुधार द्रव का प्रयोग करना सख्त वर्जित है और यह गंभीर वित्तीय अनियमितता मानी जाती है। यदि कोई लिपिकीय या गणना त्रुटि हो जाती है, तो निर्धारित नियम यह है कि गलत प्रविष्टि को लाल स्याही से एक सीधी रेखा खींचकर इस प्रकार काटा जाए कि मूल अंक पठनीय रहे, उसके ठीक ऊपर सही अंक लिखा जाए, तथा आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) अपने दिनांकित आद्याक्षर (Dated Initials) द्वारा उस सुधार को सत्यापित करे। पृष्ठ फाड़ना सरकारी नियमों के अंतर्गत दंडनीय अपराध है।

questions.explanation_english: Section 2(e) of the Delhi School Education Act (DSEAR), 1973 defines the 'Appropriate Authority'. For schools run or aided by the Delhi Administration, it is the Director of Education; for schools run or aided by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, it is the MCD Commissioner/Education Officer; and for NDMC schools, it is the New Delhi Municipal Council. Under Sections 3, 4, 5, and related rules of DSEAR 1973, the Appropriate Authority exercises statutory powers to regulate schooling, grant, renew, or withdraw school recognition, approve schemes of management for private unaided and aided schools, monitor terms and conditions of service for teachers and staff, and enforce compliance with state educational laws. The evaluation of board answer scripts is the mandate of CBSE, and textbook publication is overseen by NCERT/SCERT, making option A the correct choice.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम (DSEAR), 1973 की धारा 2(e) के तहत 'उपयुक्त प्राधिकारी' (Appropriate Authority) को परिभाषित किया गया है। दिल्ली प्रशासन द्वारा संचालित या सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों के मामले में शिक्षा निदेशक (Director of Education); दिल्ली नगर निगम (MCD) के मामले में आयुक्त; तथा एनडीएमसी (NDMC) के मामले में परिषद 'उपयुक्त प्राधिकारी' होती है। अधिनियम की धारा 3, 4 एवं 5 के तहत उपयुक्त प्राधिकारी को विद्यालयों को वैधानिक मान्यता (Recognition) प्रदान करने, उसे नवीनीकृत करने अथवा नियम उल्लंघन पर वापस लेने, प्रबंधन योजनाओं (Scheme of Management) को अनुमोदित करने, शुल्क संरचना की निगरानी करने और कर्मचारियों की सेवा शर्तों के अनुपालन को लागू करने की संपूर्ण विधिक शक्तियां प्राप्त हैं। बोर्ड परीक्षाएं कराना सीबीएसई का तथा पाठ्यपुस्तक मुद्रण एनसीईआरटी/एससीईआरटी का कार्य है।

questions.question_english: Identify the INCORRECT pair regarding the provisions under the Central Civil Services (CCS) (Leave) Rules, 1972:
options_english: Paternity Leave – Admissible for up to 15 days during wife's confinement
Maternity Leave – Admissible for up to 180 days to a female government servant
Half Pay Leave (HPL) – Credited at the rate of 20 days for each completed year of service
Extraordinary Leave (EOL) – Admissible and granted exclusively on medical grounds
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 32 of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, Extraordinary Leave (EOL) is granted to a government servant under special circumstances:
1. When no other leave is admissible by rule; or
2. When other leave is admissible, but the government servant applies in writing for the grant of extraordinary leave.
EOL is NOT granted exclusively on medical grounds. It can be sanctioned on private affairs, higher studies/scientific training in public interest, or civil unrest, subject to prescribed limits. Medical grounds are merely one of the permissible grounds.
Options (a), (b), and (c) are all correct statutory provisions:
- Rule 43-A: Paternity leave is admissible for 15 days to a male employee with less than two surviving children.
- Rule 43: Maternity leave is admissible for up to 180 days.
- Rule 29: Half Pay Leave is credited at the rate of 20 days for each completed year of service (10 days on 1st January and 10 days on 1st July).
Therefore, pair (d) is incorrect and forms the right answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (अवकाश) नियम [CCS (Leave) Rules], 1972 के नियम 32 के अंतर्गत 'असाधारण अवकाश' (EOL) विशेष परिस्थितियों में प्रदान किया जाता है:
1. जब कर्मचारी के खाते में कोई अन्य अवकाश शेष न हो; अथवा
2. अन्य अवकाश देय होने पर भी कर्मचारी स्वयं लिखित रूप में असाधारण अवकाश के लिए आवेदन करे।
असाधारण अवकाश केवल चिकित्सीय आधार तक ही सीमित नहीं है। इसे निजी कार्यों, उच्च शिक्षा, लोकहित में विशिष्ट प्रशिक्षण आदि के लिए भी सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा स्वीकृत किया जा सकता है।
अन्य तीनों विकल्प नियमानुसार पूर्णतः सही हैं:
- नियम 43-क: पितृत्व अवकाश 15 दिन के लिए देय है।
- नियम 43: मातृत्व अवकाश 180 दिनों के लिए देय है।
- नियम 29: अर्ध वेतन अवकाश (HPL) प्रतिवर्ष 20 दिन (10 दिन जनवरी व 10 दिन जुलाई) अग्रिम जमा होता है।
अतः युग्म (D) गलत होने के कारण सही उत्तर है।

questions.explanation_english: The Directorate of Education, GNCTD, provides an established, multi-tiered institutional hierarchy and statutory framework for employee grievance redressal. Legitimate channels include: (i) written representation to the Head of School (HoS) through proper channel; (ii) appeal to the Zonal DDE or District DDE; (iii) institutional grievance portals like Delhi Govt PGMS (Public Grievance Monitoring System) and central CPGRAMS; and (iv) statutory tribunals like the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT). Under Rules 19 and 20 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, government employees are strictly prohibited from bypassing departmental channels, canvassing non-official influence, or petitioning foreign governments/international organizations like the UNHRC for personal service grievances.

questions.question_english: According to rules regarding the admission of students belonging to the EWS (Economically Weaker Section) and DG (Disadvantaged Group) in private unaided recognized schools, what percentage of seats at the entry-level must be reserved?
questions.explanation_english: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 mandates that all private unaided recognized schools (excluding minority institutions protected under Article 30(1) of the Constitution) must reserve at least twenty-five percent (25%) of their seats at the entry level (pre-school/nursery, pre-primary/KG, or Class I) for children belonging to Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Disadvantaged Groups (DG) residing in the neighborhood. These students must be provided free and compulsory education until the completion of elementary education. In Delhi, the Directorate of Education (DoE) strictly regulates this process through a centralized online computerized lottery system (computerized draw of lots) to guarantee transparency, while the government reimburses schools per-child expenditure under Section 12(2) of the RTE Act.
questions.explanation_hindi: शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम (RTE Act), 2009 की धारा 12(1)(c) के अनुसार, सभी निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त मान्यता प्राप्त विद्यालयों को अपनी प्रवेश-स्तर की कक्षा (नर्सरी/केजी या कक्षा 1) की कुल स्वीकृत सीटों का कम से कम पच्चीस प्रतिशत (25%) भाग पड़ोस के आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग (EWS) और वंचित समूहों (Disadvantaged Groups - DG) के बच्चों के लिए आरक्षित रखना अनिवार्य है। इन बच्चों को प्रारंभिक शिक्षा पूर्ण होने तक निःशुल्क एवं अनिवार्य शिक्षा प्रदान की जाती है। दिल्ली में शिक्षा निदेशालय (DoE) इस 25% कोटे (जिसमें 22% EWS/DG तथा 3% दिव्यांग बच्चों/CWSN के लिए शामिल होता है) में पारदर्शी कम्प्यूटरीकृत ऑनलाइन लॉटरी (Draw of Lots) के माध्यम से विद्यालय आवंटित करता है। राज्य सरकार धारा 12(2) के तहत प्रति-बच्चा व्यय के आधार पर विद्यालयों को निर्धारित प्रतिपूर्ति (Reimbursement) प्रदान करती है।

questions.question_english: When audit inspection reports and audit objections raised by the Directorate of Audit (GNCTD) or the Principal Accountant General (Audit) / DGACR are not settled by the Head of School within the prescribed timeframe due to serious, unresolved financial irregularities, the audit para is escalated and converted into:
options_english: A statutory legislative decree
A Draft Paragraph / Public Accounts Committee (PAC) para
A Public Interest Litigation in the High Court
A suo moto contempt notice by the Supreme Court
questions.explanation_english: Under government auditing standards and Financial Rules, when inspection audit parties (from the Comptroller & Auditor General / DGACR or Directorate of Audit, GNCTD) detect serious non-compliance, financial misappropriation, or procedural violations, they issue an Inspection Report (IR) containing audit paras. The Head of School / DDO is obligated to furnish prompt, point-wise compliance replies along with supporting documentary evidence within the stipulated time limit (usually 4 to 6 weeks). If replies are not furnished or are unsatisfactory and the financial irregularity is grave, the audit authority escalates the audit objection into a 'Draft Paragraph' (Draft Para). Draft Paras are incorporated into the CAG's formal Audit Report, which is tabled in the Legislative Assembly and scrutinized intensely by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), leading to personal accountability and disciplinary proceedings against the erring HoS/DDO.
questions.explanation_hindi: लेखापरीक्षा मानकों एवं सामान्य वित्तीय नियमों के अनुसार, जब बाहरी या आंतरिक ऑडिट (CAG / DGACR या स्थानीय लेखापरीक्षा निदेशालय) द्वारा स्कूल के निरीक्षण के दौरान गंभीर वित्तीय अनियमितताएं या नियमों का उल्लंघन पाया जाता है, तो निरीक्षण रिपोर्ट (IR) में ऑडिट पैरा दर्ज किए जाते हैं। विद्यालय प्रमुख / डीडीओ (DDO) का यह दायित्व है कि वह निर्धारित समयसीमा (प्रायः 4 से 6 सप्ताह) के भीतर साक्ष्यों सहित इन आपत्तियों का बिंदुवार अनुपालन प्रस्तुत कर इनका निस्तारण करवाए। यदि गंभीर अनियमितताओं का संतोषजनक समाधान नहीं होता, तो इन आपत्तियों को 'ड्राफ्ट पैरा' (Draft Paragraph) में तब्दील कर दिया जाता है। ये ड्राफ्ट पैरा सीएजी की वार्षिक रिपोर्ट में शामिल होकर विधानसभा में पेश होते हैं और लोक लेखा समिति (PAC) के समक्ष जांच का विषय बनते हैं, जिससे संबंधित डीडीओ/अधिकारी के विरुद्ध विभागीय व अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई हो सकती है।
